deltas.behavior_text: The adaptor config loads from JSON (t3) AND from TOML via a LoadTOML front end (t9), sharing one validator; --adaptor accepts either by extension.
caused_by: d1 (proposed deviation: JSON first for in-wave file disjointness)

deltas.behavior_text: Admission is total (Reachy semantics): a newcomer is always admitted and contention it cannot win resolves per tick; MicroDuck's refusal of a newcomer sharing a channel with an unstoppable/stopping incumbent is NOT an engine behaviour — the consumer reads AdmitResult.Blocked and evicts (issue #8).

A panicking tick-seam rider or event consumer is recovered as one named senselog drop and counted in Stats.SeamPanics; the engine keeps ticking (issue #9). The donor let a raising rider propagate out of the loop.

Event-keyed rules resolve on source/type only and are routing metadata plus a one-tick sense field; priority and urgency never feed arbitration; reachy_nova's three payload-conditional rule/fire:<id> overrides are not representable and were omitted from the transcription (issue #7).

Rule-fired behaviors default to the stoppable contention class; a one-shot react rule with no duration_s falls back to the action's longest trajectory; the hysteresis re-arm reason token is 'rearming' (donor verbatim); say is forwarded as an event field with no speech actuator in the engine (issue #11).

The composition root gained a repeatable --provider flag; the stream flushes the settling neutral pose before the end frame; stdio mode has an automated end-to-end test; closing the child's stdin ends the engine with exit 0 and an end frame (reason stdin-closed) while a socket peer leaving keeps the engine running (deviations d2, d3).
The donor-literal guard matches whole literals and exempts three rules-schema keywords and one wire token (pose) via testdata lists that forbid exempting channel or action names (issues #6, #13).
The Python test job in CI builds the Go engine and exports NEUROSYMBOLIC_ENGINE so the 17 engine-backed tests and the end-to-end tests run instead of skipping (issue #10).
